hero.intro: Heat-transfer tube for the Gulf's gas plants, refineries, power and desalination plants: finned, seamless, U-bend and copper-alloy tube, with the tube sheets and exchanger parts around it.

guidance.heading: Start from the standard, the grade and the wall
guidance.body: Heat-exchanger and boiler tube is specified by its standard (ASTM A179, A192, A213, B111 and so on), the grade within it, the outside diameter and the wall, given as a BWG gauge or in millimetres and as a minimum or an average wall. Finned tube adds the fin type, material, height, thickness and density. U-bends add the bend radii and the leg lengths. Send those, the length and the quantity, and we quote against them.

standards.heading: Standards we supply against
standards.body: Carbon and alloy boiler and exchanger tube to ASTM A179, A192, A210, A213 and A209, EN 10216-2, BS 3059, JIS G3461/G3462 and GB/T 3087/5310. Stainless to ASTM A213, A269, A249, A268 and A789. Feedwater-heater U-tubes to ASTM A688, A556 and A803. Copper alloys to ASTM B111, B395, B359 and EN 12451. Pipe to ASTM A53, A106 and A333, API 5L and API 5CT. Air-cooled exchanger tube and fin to API 661 / ISO 13706.

items.q: Do the tubes come with mill test certificates?
items.a: Yes. Tubes ship with the mill's test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request, and third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan.

items.q: Can you supply sizes that are not in the size tables?
items.a: Yes. The tables list typical sizes for each range, not a full mill list. Other diameters, walls, fin geometries and lengths are made to order.

items.q: Do you build exchangers and tube sheets as well as tube?
items.a: Tube sheets, baffles and support plates are listed with their geometry. Exchangers, bundles and boiler pressure parts are built to your data sheet or drawing; send it and we quote.

hero.intro: Fin tubes for air coolers, economisers, HRSGs and fired heaters, chosen by fin type, base tube and fin geometry.

guidance.heading: Choose the fin type by temperature and atmosphere
guidance.body: Wrapped aluminium fins (L, LL, KL) suit moderate temperatures; the typical maker limit runs from about 120–150 °C for L-foot to about 260 °C for KL. Embedded G-fins take the highest temperature of the aluminium fins, about 400 °C, but leave steel exposed between the fins. Extruded fins fully sleeve the base tube and resist coastal and offshore atmospheres. Welded steel fins and studs go where flue gas is hot or dirty, and their limit is set by the fin material.

items.q: Which fin type is best for a coastal or offshore air cooler?
items.a: Extruded aluminium fins, because the fin sleeve covers the base tube completely and leaves no crevice at the fin root. LL overlapped fins also cover the tube fully.

items.q: What do I need to specify for a finned tube?
items.a: The base tube standard, grade, OD and wall; the fin type and material; fin height, thickness and fins per inch; the finned length and the bare ends at each end; and the quantity.

guidance.heading: Order tube by OD and wall, pipe by NPS and schedule
guidance.body: Heat-exchanger and boiler tube is ordered by outside diameter and wall, the wall usually given as a BWG gauge and as a minimum wall. Pipe is ordered by nominal pipe size and schedule under ASME B36.10M. Name the standard and grade; the grade decides the temperature and pressure the tube is fit for.

items.q: What is the difference between minimum wall and average wall?
items.a: A minimum-wall tube may be thicker than ordered but never thinner; an average-wall tube may vary either side of the figure within the standard's tolerance. Boiler and exchanger standards such as ASTM A179 and A192 are minimum wall unless the order says otherwise.
Yes. Tube is supplied in random or fixed lengths, typically up to about 12 m, and cut to length on request.

guidance.heading: Send the bend schedule
guidance.body: A U-tube bundle is ordered as a bend schedule: for each row, the tube size, the centreline bend radius and the leg length. Tight bends down to 1.5 × OD are available; dimensional tolerances are guaranteed from 2 × OD. Wall thinning at the bend is held to the specification on the order, and bends are stress-relieved or solution-annealed when the order asks for it.

items.q: How tight can a U-bend be?
items.a: A centreline radius of 1.5 × the tube OD can be bent. Bend tolerances are guaranteed from 2 × OD; below that, ovality and wall thinning need agreeing on the order.
To order. The bend and about 150 mm of each leg are stress-relieved or solution-annealed under ASTM A688, or a longer length where your project specification asks for it.

hero.intro: Condenser, cooler and HVAC tube in copper and its alloys, chosen by the cooling water and its velocity.

guidance.heading: Choose the alloy by the cooling water
guidance.body: Admiralty brass suits clean fresh and brackish cooling water at moderate velocity, about 1.8 m/s. Aluminium brass tolerates higher velocity than admiralty. 90/10 copper-nickel is the usual seawater condenser alloy, at 2.4–2.5 m/s in tube, and 70/30 takes more again. Copper is for HVAC, refrigeration and plumbing.

items.q: What standard covers copper-alloy condenser tubes?
items.a: ASTM B111 for straight tubes and B395 for U-bends, with EN 12451 in Europe. Low-fin tube is ASTM B359.

items.q: Are brass condenser tubes stress-relief tested?
items.a: Yes. Admiralty and aluminium brass tubes are tested for residual stress, by the mercurous nitrate test (B154) or the ammonia vapour test (B858).

products.title: High-Frequency Welded Spiral Fin Tubes — Solid and Serrated
products.descriptionShort: Steel fin strip welded helically to the base tube by high-frequency resistance welding, in a solid fin or a serrated (segmented) fin. Made to API 560, ASTM A106, ASTM A192. Supplied from Dubai with an Indus part number for each size and mill test certificates on request.
products.descriptionLong:
Steel fin strip welded helically to the base tube by high-frequency resistance welding, in a solid fin or a serrated (segmented) fin. The weld makes the fin part of the tube, so these fins carry the high gas temperatures of HRSGs, economisers and fired-heater convection sections, where the fin material, not the bond, sets the limit.

Specification

  • Maximum service temperature: Set by fin material; fired-heater fin-tip limits per API 560: carbon steel 454 °C, 2¼Cr / 5Cr 549 °C, 25Cr-20Ni 982 °C

  • Fin material: Carbon steel, low-alloy (Cr-Mo, 11–13Cr), stainless
  • Max length (m): 18.3 (60 ft)
  • Fin height, solid (mm): 9.5–31.75 (3/8–1 1/4 in)
  • Fin thickness, solid (mm): 0.89–3.05 (0.035–0.120 in)
  • Fin density, solid: 1–6 FPI (39–236 fins/m)
  • Fin height, serrated (mm): 12.7–31.75 (1/2–1 1/4 in)
  • Fin thickness, serrated (mm): 0.89–1.65 (0.035–0.065 in)
  • Fin density, serrated: 1–6 FPI (39–236 fins/m)
  • Segment width (mm): 4.0 or 7.9 (5/32 or 5/16 in)
  • Unserrated base (mm): ≈5–6.35
  • HRSG economiser base OD: 50.8 mm (2 in) is the usual standard

Standards

API 560, ASTM A106, ASTM A192, ASTM A210, ASTM A213, ASTM A335. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Materials

  • Tube: CS A106 B, A192, A210; Cr-Mo A213 T5/T9/T11/T22, A335 P5/P9/P11/P22; Stainless A312/A213 TP304H/321/347
  • Fins: Carbon steel; 11–13Cr (Type 405/410S); 18Cr-8Ni; 25Cr-20Ni

Testing and documents

  • Base tube hydrotest per its spec
  • Weld-bond / fin pull and visual checks per maker; no public standard value found
  • Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan

Where it is used

  • Fired-heater convection sections in refineries
  • Gas-fired heater convection banks
  • HRSG economisers and evaporators in GCC combined-cycle and IWPP plants
  • HRSG superheaters, evaporators and economisers in combined-cycle power and water plants

products.title: Embedded G-Fin Tubes
products.descriptionShort: Fin strip wound into a helical groove cut in the base tube, with the groove edges rolled back to lock the fin root. Made to API 661 / ISO 13706, ASTM A179, ASTM A192. Supplied from Dubai with an Indus part number for each size and mill test certificates on request.
products.descriptionLong:
Fin strip wound into a helical groove cut in the base tube, with the groove edges rolled back to lock the fin root. Embedded fins are the highest-temperature aluminium-fin type, so they go on the hot inlet passes of air coolers in refineries and gas plants. The groove takes wall from the tube, so the base tube is heavier than for wrapped fins.

Specification

  • Maximum service temperature: ≈400 °C typical maker limit (published 380–415 °C)
  • Base tube OD (mm): 12.7–50.8 (standard table 5/8–1 1/2 in)
  • Base tube wall (mm): ≥2.11; must be thicker than for wrap-on fins because the groove removes wall
  • Groove depth (mm): ≈0.4
  • Fin height (mm): 9.5–16 (3/8, 1/2, 5/8 in)
  • Fin thickness (mm): 0.38–0.51 (0.015/0.016/0.020 in); range 0.3–0.65
  • Fin density: 6–12 FPI (236–472 fins/m)
  • Fin material: Aluminium (1060/1100), copper; carbon steel possible
  • Bond type: Strip wound into a helical groove; groove edges peened/rolled back to lock the fin root
  • Max length (m): 15–18
  • Atmospheric corrosion resistance: Low: exposed steel between fins

Standards

API 661 / ISO 13706, ASTM A179, ASTM A192, ASTM A210, ASTM A106 B. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Materials

  • Tube: Carbon steel A179, A192, SA210 A1/C, A106 B; Stainless TP304/304L, TP316/316L; Duplex S31803; Copper C12200, Cu-Ni 90/10, 70/30
  • Fins: Aluminium 1060/1100; Copper; Carbon steel

Testing and documents

  • Base tube tests per its spec
  • Fin pull-out/bond check per maker QA
  • Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan

Where it is used

  • Cyclic-temperature ACHE services where owner specs call for embedded fins
  • High-temperature ACHE inlet passes (above ~315 °C) in refineries and gas plants

Sizes

5 sizes, each under its own Indus part number in the size table. The table lists typical sizes for the range; other sizes are made on request.

Ordering

Quote the Indus part number from the size table, or send the standard and grade, the outside diameter and wall (BWG or millimetres, minimum or average wall), the length and the quantity, with the fin type, material, height, thickness and fins per inch, and the bare length at each end. We quote with the mill certificates and the inspection you need.

Made to API 661 / ISO 13706, ASTM A179 / ASME SA179, SA334 Gr 6, ASME SA210. Supplied from Dubai with an Indus part number for each size and mill test certificates on request.
products.descriptionLong:
Aluminium fins extruded out of a thick aluminium sleeve over a steel, stainless or copper-alloy liner tube. The sleeve covers the liner completely and leaves no crevice at the fin root, so extruded fins are the usual choice for air coolers in coastal, offshore and humid Gulf plants.

Specification

  • Maximum service temperature: 285 °C typical maker limit (published 280–315 °C)
  • Base tube OD (mm): 12.7–50.8 (1/2–2 in); 25.4 (1 in) most common in ACHE
  • Standard base ODs (in): 1, 1 1/4, 1 1/2
  • Base (liner) tube wall, carbon steel (mm): 2.11 (14 BWG) minimum per API 661
  • Fin OD (mm): 38.1–76.2 (1 1/2–3 in)
  • Fin height (mm): 9.8–16
  • Fin thickness (mm): 0.3–0.65 (common 0.3/0.35/0.4)
  • Fin density: 5–12 FPI (197–472 fins/m); 10 FPI (394 fins/m) typical
  • Fin material: Aluminium 1100 (also 1050/1060)
  • Max length (m): 15–18
  • Atmospheric corrosion resistance: High: sleeve covers the liner tube, so no crevice at the fin root

Standards

API 661 / ISO 13706, ASTM A179 / ASME SA179, SA334 Gr 6, ASME SA210. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Materials

  • Tube: Carbon steel SA179, SA334 Gr 6; Stainless, duplex, titanium, copper alloys (liner of almost any material)
  • Fins: Aluminium 1100; Aluminium 1050/1060

Testing and documents

  • Fin bond: HTRI found bond resistance is not negligible even on new tubes
  • Liner tube hydrostatic/NDT per its base spec (A179/A334)
  • Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan

Where it is used

  • Air-cooled heat exchangers in gas processing, LNG (MR and propane coolers), gas compression stations and refineries
  • Coastal and offshore air coolers, where extruded fins are preferred for atmospheric corrosion

Sizes

We quote with the mill certificates and the inspection you need.

products.descriptionShort: Seamless chrome-moly tubes for superheaters, reheaters and high-temperature exchangers, to ASTM A213 T-grades (T11, T22, T91 and others), A209 and EN 10216-2. Made to ASTM A213 / SA-213, ASTM A209 / SA-209, ASTM A1016. Supplied from Dubai with an Indus part number for each size and mill test certificates on request.
products.descriptionLong:
Seamless chrome-moly tubes for superheaters, reheaters and high-temperature exchangers, to ASTM A213 T-grades (T11, T22, T91 and others), A209 and EN 10216-2. The grade sets the temperature: higher chrome and molybdenum carry the tube further into the creep range.

Specification

  • ASTM A213 size scope: ID 3.2 mm to OD 127 mm; min wall 0.4–12.7 mm (other sizes permitted)
  • T91 heat treatment: Normalize 1040–1080 °C + temper 730–800 °C; anneal not permitted
  • T11/T22 tensile: 415 MPa min, 205 MPa yield, 30% elongation; 163 HBW max
  • EN 10216-2 alloy delivery condition: 16Mo3 +N; 13CrMo4-5 and 10CrMo9-10 +NT
  • Equivalent grades (indicative): T1/T1a ≈ 16Mo3/15Mo3 ≈ STBA12/13; T11/T12 ≈ 13CrMo4-5 (13CrMo44) ≈ STBA23/STBA22 ≈ BS 3604 / 3059-2 620-460; T22 ≈ 10CrMo9-10 (10CrMo910) ≈ STBA24 ≈ BS 3059-2 622-490; T9 ≈ X11CrMo9-1 ≈ STBA26; T91 ≈ X10CrMoVNb9-1 ≈ STBA28 (indicative — check each tender)
  • Max service temperature (indicative): 13CrMo4-5 class about 550–560 °C; 10CrMo9-10 class about 575–580 °C; 9Cr-1Mo-V (T91) class up to about 650 °C
  • OD tolerance, cold-finished seamless and welded tube (mm): <25.4: ±0.10; 25.4–38.1: ±0.15; >38.1–<50.8: ±0.20; 50.8–<63.5: ±0.25; 63.5–<76.2: ±0.30; 76.2–101.6: ±0.38
  • Wall tolerance, cold-finished minimum-wall tube: 0/+20% for OD ≤38.1 mm; 0/+22% for OD >38.1 mm
  • Wall tolerance, hot-finished minimum-wall tube: ≤2.4 mm: 0/+40%; 2.4–3.8: 0/+35%; 3.8–4.6: 0/+33%; >4.6: 0/+28%
  • Hydrostatic test pressure: P = 32000·t/D psi (220.6·t/D MPa), capped by A450 Table 7 (highest cap 4500 psi / 31 MPa)

Standards

ASTM A213 / SA-213, ASTM A209 / SA-209, ASTM A1016, EN 10216-2, DIN 17175 (superseded by EN 10216-2), GB/T 5310, JIS G3462, BS 3059. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Materials

  • Tube: A213 T5/T9/T11/T12/T22/T91; A209 T1/T1a/T1b; 16Mo3; 13CrMo4-5; 10CrMo9-10; 15CrMoG; 12Cr1MoVG

Testing and documents

  • A213: heat and product analysis, tensile, hardness, flattening, flaring, hydrostatic or NDT (E213/E309/E570)
  • Mills recommend combining two NDT methods (UT to E213 and eddy current to E309) for A209/A213
  • Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan

Where it is used

  • Fired-heater and refinery boiler superheater coils
  • HRSG superheaters and reheaters in combined-cycle power and desalination plants

Sizes

10 sizes, each under its own Indus part number in the size table. These are the common sizes; others are made on request.

Ordering

Quote the Indus part number from the size table, or send the standard and grade, the outside diameter and wall (BWG or millimetres, minimum or average wall), the length and the quantity. We quote with the mill certificates and the inspection you need.

products.title: Stainless Steel Heat Exchanger Tubes
products.descriptionShort: Seamless and welded austenitic stainless tubes in TP304, 304L, 316, 316L, 321 and 347, with duplex to ASTM A789, for heat exchangers, condensers and feedwater heaters. Made to ASTM A213 / ASME SA-213, ASTM A269, ASTM A249 / ASME SA-249. Supplied from Dubai with an Indus part number for each size and mill test certificates on request.
products.descriptionLong:
Seamless and welded austenitic stainless tubes in TP304, 304L, 316, 316L, 321 and 347, with duplex to ASTM A789, for heat exchangers, condensers and feedwater heaters. Ordered by OD and BWG wall, as minimum or average wall.

Specification

  • ASTM A213 size scope (as usually furnished): ID 3.2 mm (1/8 in) to OD 127 mm (5 in); min wall 0.4–12.7 mm (0.015–0.500 in); average wall if ordered
  • ASTM A269 size scope: ID 6.4 mm (1/4 in) and larger, nominal wall 0.51 mm (0.020 in) and heavier; mechanical tests not required below 3.2 mm ID or 0.38 mm wall
  • ASTM A249 (welded) size scope: ID 3.2 mm to OD 304.8 mm (12 in); wall 0.4–8.1 mm (0.015–0.320 in)
  • ASTM A312 product: Seamless, straight-seam welded and heavily cold-worked welded austenitic pipe; H grades for creep service; wall tolerance −12.5 % (table by t/D)
  • ASTM A789 (duplex tube) basis: Average wall (or minimum wall if ordered); aimed at stress-corrosion-cracking resistance
  • Solution anneal, A213/A269/A249 300-series: 1040 °C (1900 °F) minimum, water quench or other rapid cool; H and stabilised grades have own minimums
  • Hardness max, TP304/304L/316/316L/321/347: 192 HBW / 200 HV / 90 HRB
  • OD tolerance, cold-finished seamless and welded tube (A1016): Under 25.4 mm: +0.10/−0.11 mm; 25.4–38.1 mm: ±0.15 mm; 38.1–50.8 mm: ±0.20 mm (includes out-of-round)
  • Wall tolerance, min-wall tube (A1016): Seamless cold-finished ≤38.1 mm OD: +20/−0 %; over 38.1 mm: +22/−0 %; welded: +18/−0 %
  • Wall tolerance, A269 (nominal wall): ±15 % under 12.7 mm OD; ±10 % from 12.7 mm upward; OD ±0.13 mm up to 38.1 mm
  • Hydrostatic test pressure (A1016 general requirement): P = 220.6·t/D MPa (32 000·t/D psi); need not exceed 7 MPa (1000 psi); hold ≥5 s; may replace or be replaced by electric NDE
  • Mill OD range for stainless HX tube: 12–88.9 mm OD (group); individual mills 12.7–25.4, 15–58, 19–88.9 mm
  • BWG to mm: 20 = 0.89; 18 = 1.24; 16 = 1.65; 14 = 2.11; 12 = 2.77; 10 = 3.40 mm
  • Most-requested stainless HX sizes: 19.05 × 1.65, 19.05 × 2.11, 25.4 × 1.65, 25.4 × 2.11 mm

Standards

ASTM A213 / ASME SA-213, ASTM A269, ASTM A249 / ASME SA-249, ASTM A312, ASTM A789, ASTM A790, ASTM A1016, BS 3059. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Materials

  • Tube: TP304/304L; TP316/316L; TP321; TP347; S31803; S32205; S32750

Testing and documents

  • A249 adds reverse-bend/flange tests on welded tube; optional weld-decay test S7
  • Flattening, flaring, hardness, tension per A213/A1016
  • Hydrostatic per A1016 (P = 220.6 t/D MPa, max 7 MPa needed, 5 s hold) or electric NDE (eddy current/ultrasonic)
  • Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan

Where it is used

  • Crude/vacuum overhead condensers — duplex/super duplex
  • Naphthenic-acid service — 317L or 316L with ≥2.5 % Mo
  • Offshore platform exchangers in chloride service — duplex/super duplex
  • Refinery hydrotreater REAC/FEAC coolers and amine coolers — duplex 2205/2507 and Alloy 825
  • Sour-water strippers and interstage coolers with chloride cooling water — duplex

Sizes

23 sizes, each under its own Indus part number in the size table. The table lists typical sizes for the range; other sizes are made on request.

Ordering

Quote the Indus part number from the size table, or send the standard and grade, the outside diameter and wall (BWG or millimetres, minimum or average wall), the length and the quantity. We quote with the mill certificates and the inspection you need.

products.descriptionLong:
U-tubes bent from seamless chrome-moly ASTM A213 T-grade and A209 tube, for high-temperature exchangers and feedwater heaters, to your bend schedule.

Specification

  • Minimum bend radius: 1.5×OD centreline radius available; dimensional tolerances guaranteed from 2×OD
  • Wall thinning at the bend: Per the governing specification on the order (ASTM A688 / TEMA, or A556 / B395) — no single percentage
  • Bend heat treatment: To order: stress-relief or solution anneal of the bend plus ~150 mm of leg (A688), or ≥300 mm where the project specification requires
  • Leg length: Up to ~12 m typical; straight tube up to 30 m on request
  • Base tube: U-bends are bent from straight A213 T-grade or A209 tube
  • A213 straight-tube scope: ID 3.2 mm to OD 127 mm; min wall 0.4–12.7 mm

Standards

ASTM A213 / SA-213, ASTM A209, ASTM A1016, DIN 17175 (superseded by EN 10216-2), EN 10216-2. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Materials

  • Tube: A213 T11; A213 T22; A209 T1; A209 T1a

Testing and documents

  • Straight-tube tests per A213/A1016; post-bend heat treatment of Cr-Mo bends not researched
  • Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan

Where it is used

  • Feedwater heaters and HX bundles in power plants

Sizes

12 sizes, each under its own Indus part number in the size table. The table lists typical sizes for the range; other sizes are made on request.

Ordering

Quote the Indus part number from the size table, or send the standard and grade, the outside diameter and wall (BWG or millimetres, minimum or average wall), the length and the quantity, with the bend schedule: centreline radius and leg length for each row, and any heat treatment of the bends. products.descriptionLong:

Specification

  • ASTM A179 size scope: OD 3.2–76.2 mm (1/8–3 in); seamless, cold drawn
  • ASTM A179 max hardness: 72 HRB
  • ASTM A192 max hardness: 137 HB (wall ≥5.1 mm) / 77 HRB
  • ASTM A210 max hardness: A-1: 79 HRB / 143 HB; C: 89 HRB / 179 HB
  • Common heat-exchanger tube ODs: 15.88, 19.05, 25.40, 31.75, 38.10, 50.80 mm (5/8, 3/4, 1, 1-1/4, 1-1/2, 2 in)
  • Cold-drawn minimum-wall tube range: 12.70×0.89 to 76.20×5.59 mm (0.500×0.035 to 3.000×0.220 in, 20–5 BWG)
  • GB/T 3087 general length: 4–12.5 m

Low fins rolled out of the tube wall itself, with plain ends left unfinned. The fin tips are no larger than the plain-end OD, so the tubes fit the same tube-sheet and baffle holes as plain tube while carrying several times the outside surface. Used in condensers, chillers and shell-and-tube exchangers where the shell side limits the duty.

  • Plain-end OD (mm): 15.875–25.4 (5/8, 3/4, 7/8, 1 in)

  • Fin height 26 FPI (mm): 1.245 (0.049 in)
  • Fin height 28 FPI (mm): 0.889 (0.035 in)
  • Fin thickness avg (mm): 0.28–0.36
  • Tolerances: FPI +3/−2; fin height ±0.076 mm; transition 12.7–101.6 mm; land length ≥25.4 mm
  • Max length (m): >13.4 (length tolerance bands run past 44 ft)

Standards

Testing and documents

products.title: Studded Tubes
products.descriptionShort: Steel studs welded in rows round the tube, for fired-heater convection sections. Made to API 560, ASTM A106, ASTM A335. Supplied from Dubai with an Indus part number for each size and mill test certificates on request.
products.descriptionLong:
Steel studs welded in rows round the tube, for fired-heater convection sections. Studs shed soot and ash better than fins, so they are used on the shield rows and where the burners fire liquid or dirty fuel.

Specification

  • Maximum service temperature: Set by stud material; fired-heater stud-tip limits per API 560: carbon steel 454 °C, 2¼Cr / 5Cr 549 °C, 25Cr-20Ni 982 °C
  • Stud diameter (mm): 12.7 (1/2 in) most common
  • Stud height (mm): 25.4 (1 in) typical; max 19 for heavier liquid fuels
  • Stud row spacing (mm): 15.9 (0.625 in), i.e. ~63 rows/m (19.2 rows/ft)
  • Attachment: Each stud arc- or resistance-welded to the tube
  • Support: At least three rows of studs rest on each tube support
  • Where used: Convection section only; three rows of bare shield tubes between extended surface and the radiant firebox
  • Fuel rule: Some owner specifications: vertical convection tubes on liquid fuel must use studs, not fins

Standards

API 560, ASTM A106, ASTM A335, ASTM A312, ASTM A192, ASTM A193, ASTM A199, ASTM A213, ASTM A510. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Materials

  • Tube: A106 B; A335 P5/P9; A213 T9; A312 TP347
  • Fins: CS studs; 11–13Cr; 18Cr-8Ni; 25Cr-20Ni

Testing and documents

  • Stud weld quality per heater spec; base tube hydrotest
  • Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan

Where it is used

  • Refinery crude, vacuum and reformer heater convection sections firing fuel oil or mixed fuel

Sizes

1 size, each under its own Indus part number in the size table. The table lists typical sizes for the range; other sizes are made on request.

We quote with the mill certificates and the inspection you need.

products.descriptionShort: U-tubes in copper, admiralty and aluminium brass and copper-nickel to ASTM B395, for coolers and condensers with removable bundles. products.descriptionLong:
U-tubes in copper, admiralty and aluminium brass and copper-nickel to ASTM B395, for coolers and condensers with removable bundles. Bends are relief-annealed where the alloy needs it, and a dual-gauge tube with a heavier bend section is available.

Specification

  • Minimum bend radius: 1.5×OD centreline radius available; dimensional tolerances guaranteed from 2×OD
  • Wall thinning at the bend: Per the governing specification on the order (ASTM A688 / TEMA, or A556 / B395) — no single percentage
  • Bend heat treatment: To order: stress-relief or solution anneal of the bend plus ~150 mm of leg (A688), or ≥300 mm where the project specification requires
  • Leg length: Up to ~12 m typical; straight tube up to 30 m on request
  • Size scope: OD ≤2 in (50 mm)
  • Leg spacing tolerance: (2R − OD) ±1.6 mm (1/16 in)
  • Leg length tolerance (all plus): ≤6 m +3.2; 6–9 m +4.0; 9–18 m +6.4; >18 m +9.5 mm; leg difference ≤3.2 mm
  • Dual-gauge option: bend section one BWG heavier, constant ID; heavy section ≥100 mm long

Standards

ASTM B395/B395M, ASTM B111, ASTM B135, ASTM B68, BS 2871, BS EN12451, EN 12735-2, JIS H3300. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Materials

  • Tube: C12200 etc.; C44300–C44500; C68700; C70600/C70620; C71500/C71520; C72200

Testing and documents

  • Eddy current before bending
  • Hydrostatic at 48 MPa fibre stress (≤6.9 MPa) or pneumatic 400 kPa for 5 s, on each U-tube
  • Mercurous nitrate / ammonia vapour on bend and leg for brasses
  • Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan

Where it is used

  • U-tube feedwater heaters, coolers and chillers

Specification

  • Maximum design water velocity in tube: 90/10 Cu-Ni 2.4–2.5 m/s in condenser tube (3.5 m/s applies to large-bore pipe only); 70/30 tolerates higher velocity than 90/10

  • Tensile / yield min, C71500 (MPa): O61 360/125; HR50 495/345
  • Tensile / yield min, C71640 (MPa): O61 435/170; HR50 560/400
  • EN 12451 annealed CuNi10Fe1Mn: R290: Rm 290, Rp0.2 90 MPa, A 30%
  • Other common sizes: 5/8×0.035 in, 3/4×0.035 in, 1×0.049 in, 1×0.120 in
  • Hydrostatic test basis: fibre stress 48 MPa (7000 psi), P = 2St/(D−0.8t), not above 7.0 MPa unless specified; or pneumatic 400 kPa for 5 s; eddy current is the default NDT

Standards

ASTM B111/B111M, ASTM B359, ASTM B395, ASTM B466, EN 12451, ASTM B858, ASTM B154, BS 2871, IS 1545, JIS H 3300, NES 779. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Materials

  • Tube: C70600 / CW352H 90-10; C70620 90-10 welding grade; C71500 / CW354H 70-30; C71520 70-30 welding grade; C71640 / CW353H 66-30-2-2

Testing and documents

  • Expansion pin test B153: 30% O61, 20% H55/HR50
  • Flattening at three places to 3× wall
  • Grain size 0.010–0.045 mm for O61
  • Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan

Where it is used

  • MSF desalination heat-recovery and heat-rejection tubing; C71640 for the heat-rejection section where impingement is severe

  • Shipboard and offshore seawater coolers

  • Fin material: Aluminium 1100-O or 5052-type alloy, copper; edge-tension also CS and stainless
  • Bond type: Tension wound with an L-shaped foot; contact pressure only, which loosens with time and temperature cycling
  • Fin end retention: API 661 calls for cast zinc bands at tube ends to stop footed fins unwinding
  • Max length (m): 18

products.title: Heat Exchanger Tube Bundles
products.descriptionShort: Replacement and new tube bundles for shell-and-tube exchangers and air coolers, built from the original data sheet or a new design, for turnaround retubing and bundle replacement. Made to TEMA (R/C/B), API 660 9th ed. / ISO 16812, ASME VIII Div 1 / EN 13445. Built to your data sheet or drawing and quoted against it, with the documents and inspection your project needs.
products.descriptionLong:
Replacement and new tube bundles for shell-and-tube exchangers and air coolers, built from the original data sheet or a new design, for turnaround retubing and bundle replacement.

Most bundle orders in the Gulf come in ahead of a turnaround: the shell and channel stay in place, the old bundle is pulled, and the new one has to fit first time. Where the original tubes failed early, a change of tube material or wall, or a move to low-fin or twisted-tape tube, can be built into the new bundle at the same time.

Heat Exchanger Tube Bundles are engineered equipment, not catalogue items. We quote against your data sheet or drawing, and the design, materials, inspection and documents follow the code and the specification you give us.

How we build and quote

A replacement bundle is built to slide into the existing shell and bolt to the existing channel, so it starts from the original data sheet, the nameplate or a survey of the old bundle. We match the tube count, size, pitch and layout, the baffle arrangement and the tube-sheet thickness, or redesign the bundle where the duty or the materials have changed. Tube sheets are drilled and grooved to TEMA, tubes are expanded or welded to a qualified procedure, and the bundle is hydrotested and documented before it ships, ready for a turnaround window.

Specification

  • Retubing practice: Clean tube-hole grooves to bare metal before inserting new tubes; avoid over-rolling, which weakens ligaments and distorts the tubesheet

Standards

TEMA (R/C/B), API 660 9th ed. / ISO 16812, ASME VIII Div 1 / EN 13445, PED 2014/68/EU. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Testing and documents

  • Documentation, inspection and test plan to the order's code and specification

Where it is used

  • Gas-plant ACHE re-tubing
  • Refinery T&I bundle replacement

  • Tube count, OD, wall, length, pitch and layout
  • Baffle type, cut and spacing

products.descriptionLong:
Finned tube coils for heating, cooling and heat recovery, built to your duty and duct dimensions.

Finned coils are used for air heating and cooling in process and HVAC plant, for heat recovery from exhaust and flue gas, and as steam, hot-water or thermal-oil heating coils in ducts. The tube and fin are chosen together: copper or stainless tube with aluminium or copper fins for clean air, steel tube with steel fins for hot or dirty gas. Fin spacing is opened up where the air carries dust, and coils can be galvanised or coated for coastal sites.

Finned Tube Coils are engineered equipment, not catalogue items. We quote against your data sheet or drawing, and the design, materials, inspection and documents follow the code and the specification you give us.

How we build and quote

Coils are built to the duty and the space they go into. The tube or pipe grade, the bend radii and the coil dimensions come from the drawing or from our design for your duty; finned coils add the fin type, material and spacing. Bends are made to keep wall thinning and ovality inside the governing specification, welds are to qualified procedures, and each coil is pressure tested and documented to the inspection and test plan before it ships.

Testing and documents

  • Documentation, inspection and test plan to the order's code and specification

Where it is used

products.title: Carbon Steel and Clad Tube Sheets
products.descriptionShort: Tube sheets in SA-516-70 plate and SA-266, SA-105, SA-350 LF2 and SA-182 forgings, plain or explosion-clad and weld-overlaid, drilled, grooved and finished to your drawing and TEMA. Made to TEMA (10th ed. / 2026 ed.), ASME VIII Div 1 (Part UHX), ASTM A516. Supplied from Dubai with an Indus part number for each size and mill test certificates on request.
products.descriptionLong:
Tube sheets in SA-516-70 plate and SA-266, SA-105, SA-350 LF2 and SA-182 forgings, plain or explosion-clad and weld-overlaid, drilled, grooved and finished to your drawing and TEMA.

Specification

  • Product form by thickness: Plate (SA-516-70) for thinner sheets; forged discs (SA-266, SA-105, SA-350 LF2, SA-182) above about 100-125 mm or for high-integrity service
  • Low-temperature tubesheet material: SA-350 LF2 forging for low-temperature service (about -46 to -48 C); SA-516-70 may need normalizing and impact testing by thickness/MDMT (UCS-66)
  • SA-516-70 tensile / yield: 485-620 MPa tensile; 260 MPa min yield; elongation 21% (50 mm) / 17% (200 mm)
  • SA-516-70 normalizing: Plates over 38 mm (1.5 in) supplied normalized unless otherwise ordered
  • Cladding options: Explosion-clad (SS 304L/316L, duplex 2205/2507, Ti Gr1/2, alloy 625/825/C-276, Cu-Ni 90/10 or 70/30 on SA-516-60/70 or P265GH/P355GH) or weld overlay
  • Explosion-clad layer thickness: 3-10 mm typical for tube sheets; 1-50 mm possible; base 10-500 mm; single pieces to about 50 t; flatness within 1 mm/m
  • Clad bond inspection: 100% UT of bond per ASME SA-263 / SA-264 / SA-265 (or EN 13445-2), including after simulated PWHT
  • Explosion clad vs weld overlay: Explosion clad keeps full alloy chemistry (no dilution) and the full clad thickness is drillable and weldable; overlay adds dilution, heat input and distortion and suits small or one-off parts
  • Clad tubesheet strength welds: ASME VIII Div 1 UW-20.7 lets tube-to-tubesheet welds in integral clad be strength welds if shear test and UT are done
  • Minimum tube pitch: 1.25 x tube OD (triangular or square)
  • Square-pitch cleaning lane (mechanical cleaning): min 6.4 mm (1/4 in); 4.8 mm (3/16 in) allowed in shells <= 12 in (Class C)
  • Class C pitch exception: 1.2 x OD permitted for tubes 5/8 in and smaller with expanded joints
  • Tube layout angles: 30 deg (triangular), 60 deg (rotated triangular), 90 deg (square), 45 deg (rotated square)
  • Tubesheet hole, standard fit, 3/4 in (19.05 mm) tube: 0.760 in (19.30 mm) nominal, under-tolerance 0.004 in (0.10 mm)
  • Tubesheet hole, standard fit, 1 in (25.4 mm) tube: 1.012 in (25.70 mm) nominal, under-tolerance 0.004 in (0.10 mm)
  • Tube-hole clearance in practice: Drill and ream to 0.007-0.010 in (0.18-0.25 mm) over tube OD (heat exchangers and condensers); boiler drum / header seats about 1/32 in (0.8 mm) over OD
  • Special close fit holes: Mandatory in ACHE headers when tubes are austenitic SS, duplex SS, titanium, copper-nickel or nickel alloy (ISO 13706 / API 661 cl. 9.3.1.2)
  • Tube-hole grooving (expanded joints): Grooves for tubes 5/8 in OD and larger; 1 groove when tubesheet <= 25 mm (1 in) thick, 2 grooves when thicker; grooves about 3.2 mm (1/8 in) wide with 6.4 mm (1/4 in) between them; final size/arrangement at maker's discretion

Standards

TEMA (10th ed. / 2026 ed.), ASME VIII Div 1 (Part UHX), ASTM A516, ASTM A266, ASTM A105, ASTM A350, ASTM A182, ASTM A240, ASTM A263, ASTM A264, ASTM A265, API 660 / API 661, EN 13445-3, ASTM A387, EN 1092-1. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Testing and documents

  • Clad bond 100% UT (SA-263/264/265)
  • Hydrotest of the completed exchanger
  • Tube-to-tubesheet procedure qualification (purchaser approval under API 661)
  • Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan

Where it is used

  • Feedwater heaters and condensers in power plants
  • Refinery and gas-plant shell-and-tube exchangers (T&I replacement tube sheets)
  • Seawater coolers and desalination (clad duplex / Ti / Cu-Ni)

products.descriptionShort: Tube sheets in titanium Grades 1 and 2, solid (ASTM B265 plate, B381 forgings) or explosion-clad on carbon steel, for seawater condensers and desalination plants. products.descriptionLong:
Tube sheets in titanium Grades 1 and 2, solid (ASTM B265 plate, B381 forgings) or explosion-clad on carbon steel, for seawater condensers and desalination plants.

Specification

  • Grades: ASTM B265 plate Gr 1 / Gr 2; ASTM B381 forgings F-1 / F-2
  • Clad alternative: Ti Gr 1/2 explosion-clad on SA-516-70 for seawater condensers, desalination, PTA, chlor-alkali
  • Clad bond shear (reactive metal clad, ASTM B898): min 20,000 psi (137.9 MPa), tested only when Supplementary Requirement S1 is specified
  • Typical Ti-steel bond strength: 35,000-45,000 psi shear; backer plate usually >= 3/4 in (19 mm)
  • ACHE header choice: Bonnet headers used where the tubesheet is an expensive alloy such as titanium
  • Hole fit: Special close fit mandatory with titanium tubes in API 661 headers
  • Expansion: 4-5% wall reduction; use expanders with 4 or more rolls to limit tube-end cracking
  • Minimum tube pitch: 1.25 x tube OD (triangular or square)
  • Tube layout angles: 30 deg (triangular), 60 deg (rotated triangular), 90 deg (square), 45 deg (rotated square)

Standards

ASTM B265 / ASME SB-265, ASTM B381 / ASME SB-381, ASTM B898, ISO 2768-fH. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Specification

  • ASTM A178 tensile: C: 415/255 MPa, 30%; D: 485/275 MPa, 30%; A: design values only
  • ASTM A214 max hardness: 72 HRB
  • OD tolerance, welded tube: Same as cold-finished seamless rows of A450 Table 3 (e.g. ±0.10 mm under 25.4 mm OD)
  • Equivalence: A178 A and C are grouped with A192 / A210 A-1 / St45.8 / STB grades

products.descriptionLong:
Finned tube evaporator coils for process and refrigeration duty, built to your data sheet.

Evaporator coils boil a refrigerant or a process fluid inside the tubes while air or gas passes across the fins. The circuiting, tube size and fin spacing are set by the refrigerant, the evaporating temperature and the frosting or fouling the coil will see, and the coil is leak-tested and dried before it is sealed for shipping.

The tube or pipe grade, the bend radii and the coil dimensions come from the drawing or from our design for your duty; finned coils add the fin type, material and spacing. products.title: Heat Pipe Heat Exchangers
products.descriptionShort: Banks of sealed, finned heat pipes that move heat from a hot gas stream to a cold one with no cross-leakage between them, for flue-gas and exhaust heat recovery and HVAC energy recovery. Built to your data sheet or drawing and quoted against it, with the documents and inspection your project needs.
products.descriptionLong:
Banks of sealed, finned heat pipes that move heat from a hot gas stream to a cold one with no cross-leakage between them, for flue-gas and exhaust heat recovery and HVAC energy recovery.

Heat pipe exchangers suit duties where the two gas streams must never mix, such as combustion-air preheating from flue gas, dryer and kiln exhaust recovery, and fresh-air preheat or precool in HVAC. Because each pipe works on its own, a failed pipe does not stop the unit, and the bank can be built with the hot-side fin spacing opened up for dirty gas.

Heat Pipe Heat Exchangers are engineered equipment, not catalogue items. We quote against your data sheet or drawing, and the design, materials, inspection and documents follow the code and the specification you give us.

How we build and quote

Each heat pipe is a sealed, finned tube with a small charge of working fluid that boils at the hot end and condenses at the cold end, so heat moves along the pipe with no pumping and no leakage path between the two gas streams. The working fluid is chosen for the gas temperature, and the fin spacing and material for the fouling and the dew point of the hot stream. We size the unit from the two flows and temperatures, the allowable pressure drop and the duct space, and build it to fit the duct.

Testing and documents

  • Documentation, inspection and test plan to the order's code and specification

Where it is used

  • Flue-gas / exhaust heat recovery to combustion air
  • HVAC energy recovery

What to send for a quotation

  • Hot gas flow, inlet temperature and composition, including dew point, dust and SOx
  • Cold stream (air or water) flow and temperatures
  • Allowable pressure drop on both sides
  • Duct dimensions and orientation
  • Fin spacing and materials suited to fouling
  • Cleaning method

products.title: Shell and Tube Heat Exchangers
products.descriptionShort: Shell-and-tube heat exchangers to TEMA classes R, C and B and API 660 / ISO 16812, in fixed-tubesheet, U-tube and floating-head types, built to your process data sheet. Made to TEMA (R/C/B), API 660 9th ed. / ISO 16812, ASME VIII Div 1 / EN 13445. Built to your data sheet or drawing and quoted against it, with the documents and inspection your project needs.
products.descriptionLong:
Shell-and-tube heat exchangers to TEMA classes R, C and B and API 660 / ISO 16812, in fixed-tubesheet, U-tube and floating-head types, built to your process data sheet.

Shell and Tube Heat Exchangers are engineered equipment, not catalogue items. We quote against your data sheet or drawing, and the design, materials, inspection and documents follow the code and the specification you give us.

How we build and quote

We work from the TEMA data sheet. The thermal design sets the surface, the number of shells and passes and the tube layout; the mechanical design then follows ASME Section VIII Division 1 or EN 13445, with TEMA class R for refinery service, B for chemical and C for general duty, and API 660 / ISO 16812 where the owner specifies it. Tubes, tube sheets, baffles, shells and channels are made to the grades on the data sheet, the tube-to-tubesheet joints are expanded or welded to a qualified procedure, and each unit is hydrotested and documented to the inspection and test plan before it ships from the fabricating shop.

Specification

  • TEMA type code: 3 letters: front head (A, B, C, N, D) / shell (E, F, G, H, J, K, X) / rear head (L, M, N fixed tubesheet; P, S, T, W floating; U = U-tube). Example BEM = bonnet, one-pass shell, fixed bonnet rear
  • TEMA classes: R = refinery (most demanding), B = chemical, C = general commercial; R adds recessed/confined gasket and thicker minimums
  • API 660 edition in force: 9th edition (2015); ISO 16812:2019 supplements it
  • Common configurations: AEU/BEU: cheapest removable bundle, even tube passes only; AES/AET: costliest removable bundle; AEM/BEM/AEL: fixed tubesheet, shell side not cleanable mechanically; NEN: very high pressure

Standards

TEMA (R/C/B), API 660 9th ed. / ISO 16812, ASME VIII Div 1 / EN 13445, PED 2014/68/EU. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Testing and documents

  • Documentation, inspection and test plan to the order's code and specification

Where it is used

products.descriptionShort: Air-cooled heat exchangers (air fin coolers) to API 661 / ISO 13706, forced or induced draft, with plug, cover-plate or bonnet headers, built to your data sheet for gas plants, refineries, LNG and power plants. Made to API 661 / ISO 13706, ASME VIII Div 1, ASME PTC 30. Built to your data sheet or drawing and quoted against it, with the documents and inspection your project needs.
products.descriptionLong:
Air-cooled heat exchangers (air fin coolers) to API 661 / ISO 13706, forced or induced draft, with plug, cover-plate or bonnet headers, built to your data sheet for gas plants, refineries, LNG and power plants.

Air-Cooled Heat Exchangers are engineered equipment, not catalogue items. We quote against your data sheet or drawing, and the design, materials, inspection and documents follow the code and the specification you give us.

How we build and quote

We work from the API 661 / ISO 13706 data sheet. The thermal design sets the bundle, the number of tube rows and passes and the fan duty; the mechanical design covers the headers, the plenum, the structure and the walkways, with the site's wind, seismic and ambient conditions. Tubes, fins and headers are made to the grades on the data sheet, header welds are fully radiographed or ultrasonically tested, and each bundle is hydrotested and documented to the inspection and test plan. Replacement bundles are built to fit the existing bays.

Specification

  • Governing standard: API 661 / ISO 13706 (not API 660, which is shell-and-tube)
  • Header types: Plug header (most common; plugs opposite each tube for inspection and rolling); cover-plate header for fouling service roughly below 150 psig; bonnet header where tubesheet is costly alloy (e.g. titanium)
  • Plug holes: Plug-hole thread nominal diameter at least tube OD + 1/8 in; thread full depth of plugsheet; plug torque values with lubricant must be submitted
  • Fan coverage and dispersion: Fan area >= 40% of bundle face area; dispersion angle <= 45 deg
  • Minimum fan diameter: 3 ft (0.9 m)
  • Fan diameters offered: 5-40 ft (1.5-12.2 m); fan solutions for air outlet up to 204 C (400 F)
  • Tube OD: Preferred minimum 1.0 in; common 1.0, 1.25, 1.5 in; small packaged units use 5/8-1-1/4 in round finned tubes
  • Section length: Cooling sections 3-60 ft (0.9-18 m)
  • Header design pressure range: 150-11,150 psig (ASME) for gas-compression coolers
  • Draft: Forced draft (most units; easier maintenance, fans away from hot air) or induced draft (less hot-air recirculation)
  • Control options: VFD, variable-pitch fans, louvers, warm-air recirculation, steam coils / winterization
  • Screens: Insect/lint and hail screens mesh No. 8 (ISO 13706 cl. 7.2.11)
  • Nozzle loads (per header, plug bundles): Forces 1500 lb transverse / 2500 lb axial to bundle / 3000 lb along nozzle; moments 3000 / 2000 / 4000 ft-lb
  • Weld hardness / NDE: Weld and HAZ hardness <= 20 HRC (22 HRC for some grades); all pressure welds full penetration; all welds UT or RT
  • Performance test: If specified, per ASME PTC 30

Standards

API 661 / ISO 13706, ASME VIII Div 1, ASME PTC 30, IOGP S-710, EN 13445. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Testing and documents

  • Hardness of welds/HAZ
  • Hydrotest; drain promptly after test
  • Optional PTC 30 performance test
  • UT or RT of all header welds
  • Documentation, inspection and test plan to the order's code and specification

Where it is used

  • Gas processing and compression (gas, propane, lean amine, glycol coolers)
  • LNG liquefaction
  • Power-plant and gen-set radiators
  • Refinery overhead condensers and product coolers
  • Water-scarce sites where air cooling replaces cooling water

What to send for a quotation

  • Service, fluid, total flow and phase
  • Inlet and outlet temperatures, allowable pressure drop and fouling
  • Design pressure, design temperature, MDMT and test pressure
  • Design ambient dry-bulb temperature, minimum ambient and site elevation
  • Plot limits: bay width and length, elevation and bundle orientation
  • Forced or induced draft, header type and fan control
  • Tube material, OD, wall and length; fin type and material
  • Inspection and test plan, and any performance test

products.descriptionLong:
Pipe and tube coiled into helices for heaters, tank coils and coil-wound exchangers, from carbon steel and alloy tube and pipe.

Helical coils pack a long tube length into a small volume and are used as tank and reactor heating and cooling coils, fired-heater and waste-heat coils, and the tube side of coil-wound exchangers. The coil diameter, pitch and number of turns follow from the duty and the space, and the bend radius is kept large enough that wall thinning and ovality stay inside the tube specification.

Helical Pipe Coils are engineered equipment, not catalogue items. We quote against your data sheet or drawing, and the design, materials, inspection and documents follow the code and the specification you give us.

How we build and quote

Coils are built to the duty and the space they go into. The tube or pipe grade, the bend radii and the coil dimensions come from the drawing or from our design for your duty; finned coils add the fin type, material and spacing. Bends are made to keep wall thinning and ovality inside the governing specification, welds are to qualified procedures, and each coil is pressure tested and documented to the inspection and test plan before it ships.

Specification

  • Coil base material: Coils are formed from the same tube/pipe grades (A106, A179, A192, A210, EN 10216) covered above

Standards

ASTM A106, ASTM A179, ASTM A192, ASTM A210 / EN 10216-2, EN 10216. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Materials

  • Tube: A106 B; A179; A192; A210; P235GH; stainless (other lane)

Testing and documents

  • Documentation, inspection and test plan to the order's code and specification

Where it is used

  • Coil type and dimensions, or the drawing

products.descriptionLong:
Forged flanges to ASME B16.5 and B16.47 Series A and B, EN 1092-1 and other standards, for exchanger nozzles and large-bore cooling-water and LNG headers. Exchanger girth flanges are designed with the exchanger.

Forged Flanges for Heat Exchangers are engineered equipment, not catalogue items. We quote against your data sheet or drawing, and the design, materials, inspection and documents follow the code and the specification you give us.

How we build and quote

Standard flanges are forged and machined to the dimensional standard, the pressure class and the material grade you specify, with the bore matched to the pipe schedule for weld necks. Large-bore flanges above NPS 24 follow ASME B16.47 Series A or Series B, which are not interchangeable in most classes, so the series must be stated. Exchanger girth and body flanges are designed with the exchanger and made to its drawing. Each flange ships with its mill certificate and marking to the standard.

Specification

  • B16.47 series origin: Series A = former MSS SP-44 dimensions; Series B = former API 605 dimensions
  • API 605 status: Withdrawn; dimensions live on as ASME B16.47 Series B
  • Series A/B interchangeability: Not interchangeable in Class 150 and 300, nor NPS 36 and smaller above Class 300
  • RTJ in B16.47: Ring-type joint facing available Class 300-900, NPS 26-36
  • Gasket surface finish (ACHE): 0.8-1.6 um Ra (32-64 uin) under ISO 13706 / API 661
  • Exchanger body / girth flanges: Girth flange type and future machining allowance are separate TEMA datasheet fields; these are custom-designed, not catalogue B16.5 parts

Standards

ASME B16.5, ASME B16.47 Series A/B, MSS SP-44, EN 1092-1, ASME B16.47 Series B, ASME B16.47, DIN 2631-2638, GB/T 9112-2010, JIS B2220. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

products.descriptionShort: Segmental baffles and tube support plates for shell-and-tube exchangers, stack-drilled to TEMA hole clearances and your drawing. Made to TEMA, HEI Standards for Closed Feedwater Heaters. Supplied from Dubai with an Indus part number for each size and mill test certificates on request.
products.descriptionLong:
Segmental baffles and tube support plates for shell-and-tube exchangers, stack-drilled to TEMA hole clearances and your drawing.

Specification

  • Baffle tube-hole clearance: Tube OD + 0.8 mm (1/32 in) when unsupported span <= 914 mm or OD > 31.8 mm; OD + 0.4 mm (1/64 in) when span > 914 mm and OD <= 31.8 mm
  • Baffle-hole over-tolerance: +0.010 in (0.25 mm; TEMA metric 0.3 mm) on 96% of holes; +0.015 in (0.4 mm) on remaining 4%
  • Stack drilling: Baffles and supports are stack-drilled; stacks normally no deeper than 5 x drill diameter; drill drift about 0.0016 in per drill diameter of depth
  • Tighter holes: Specifying holes tighter than TEMA/HEI raises cost and risks tube damage at insertion; zone design, larger entrance/exit areas, larger pitch or thicker baffles control vibration better
  • Datasheet baffle fields: Cross-baffle type, cut % of diameter, vertical/horizontal cut, spacing, inlet spacing, longitudinal baffle seal, tube support type, U-bend support, bypass seals, impingement protection
  • Hole finish: Burrs removed, workmanlike finish

Standards

TEMA, HEI Standards for Closed Feedwater Heaters. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Testing and documents

  • Dimensional check of hole size against the 96% / 4% rule
  • Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan

Where it is used

products.descriptionLong:
Stainless U-tubes to ASTM A688 and A803 and carbon steel U-tubes to ASTM A556 for high- and low-pressure feedwater heaters in power and desalination plants.

Specification

  • A688 tensile TP304/316: 515 MPa / 205 MPa / 35 %

  • A688 welded tube: Automatic weld, no filler; weld (or weld and base) cold worked before final HT; reverse-bend test per 460 m

U-tubes; 15.9–25.4 mm (5/8–1 in) OD; average or minimum wall 0.7 mm (0.028 in) and heavier; A688 bend HT: Optional; same solution anneal as straight tube (≥1040 °C, rapid cool below 370 °C; N08367 1107 °C) over bend + ~150 mm per leg; inert ID purge; A688 thinning: t_f ≥ 4RT/(4R + D); A688 ovality: ≤10 % of pre-bend OD at R ≥ 2D; A688 pressure test: Each U-tube after bending/HT: hydro (A1016 or agreed) or pneumatic; A688 chloride limit: Residual chloride on tube surfaces ≤10.7 mg/m² (1 mg/ft²) at packing; one tube per 500 checked; A556 scope: Seamless cold-drawn carbon steel FWH tubes incl. U-tubes; 15.9–31.8 mm (5/8–1-1/4 in) OD; minimum wall ≥1.1 mm (0.045 in); A556 bend stress relief: If specified, heat the bent portion to 585–640 °C (1100–1200 °F); straight tube tempered ≥640 °C after last draw; A556 thinning: t_f ≥ T·2R/(2R + D) — more severe than the A688/TEMA form; A556 ovality and OD tolerance: ≤10 % at R ≥ 2D (1.5D may exceed); straight OD ±0.10 mm under 25.4 mm, ±0.15 mm 25.4–31.7 mm; wall +20/−0 %; A556 hydro: Each U-tube hydro tested (or 1.5 × design pressure by agreement); A803 scope: Ferritic stainless FWH tubes incl. U-tubes, 15.9–25.4 mm OD, wall ≥0.7 mm; straight tube for bending furnished annealed; B395 (copper-alloy U-bends, for comparison): Dual-gage option: central bend section one BWG heavier, ≥100 mm long and ≥ bend arc (+76/−0 mm); thinning t_f ≥ t·2R/(2R + D); ovality ≤10 %; leg spacing ±1.6 mm; Cu-Ni HR50 radius ≥2.2×OD (1.24 mm wall) / ≥2×OD (1.47 mm wall); brass/admiralty bends must be relief annealed, Cu-Ni bends if specified; eddy current before bending

products.title: High-Temperature Carbon Steel Pipe — ASTM A106
products.descriptionShort: Seamless carbon steel pipe to ASTM A106 Grades B and C for high-temperature service in refineries, power plants and boilers, by NPS and schedule under ASME B36.10M. Made to ASTM A106/A106M, ASME B36.10M. Supplied from Dubai with an Indus part number for each size and mill test certificates on request.
products.descriptionLong:
Seamless carbon steel pipe to ASTM A106 Grades B and C for high-temperature service in refineries, power plants and boilers, by NPS and schedule under ASME B36.10M.

Specification

  • A106 Grade B: C ≤0.30, Mn 0.29–1.06, P/S ≤0.035, Si ≥0.10; 415 MPa tensile, 240 MPa yield
  • A106 Grade C: C ≤0.35; 485 MPa tensile, 275 MPa yield

Standards

ASTM A106/A106M, ASME B36.10M. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Materials

  • Tube: A106 A; A106 B; A106 C

Testing and documents

  • Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan

Where it is used

  • Refinery, gas-plant and power-plant process and steam piping

Sizes

44 sizes, each under its own Indus part number in the size table. The sizes follow the standard's own table.

Ordering

Quote the Indus part number from the size table, or send the standard and grade, the outside diameter and wall (BWG or millimetres, minimum or average wall), the length and the quantity. We quote with the mill certificates and the inspection you need.

products.title: Low-Temperature Carbon Steel Pipe — ASTM A333
products.descriptionShort: Seamless carbon steel pipe to ASTM A333 Grades 1, 3 and 6 for low-temperature service, impact tested down to −45 °C for Grade 6, by NPS and schedule under ASME B36.10M. Made to ASTM A333/A333M, ASTM A334/A334M, ASME B36.10M. Supplied from Dubai with an Indus part number for each size and mill test certificates on request.
products.descriptionLong:
Seamless carbon steel pipe to ASTM A333 Grades 1, 3 and 6 for low-temperature service, impact tested down to −45 °C for Grade 6, by NPS and schedule under ASME B36.10M. Tube sizes to ASTM A334.

Specification

  • A333 Grade 6: C ≤0.30, Mn 0.29–1.06, P/S ≤0.025; 415 MPa tensile, 240 MPa yield, 30%; normalized
  • A333 Gr 1/6 Charpy test temperature: -45 to -46 °C (-50 °F)
  • A333 Grade 3: 3.18–3.82% Ni; 450 MPa tensile, 240 MPa yield; Charpy around -100 °C
  • Equivalence: A333 Gr 1/6 ≈ EN 10216-4 P215NL / P255QL ≈ DIN 17173 TTSt35N

Standards

ASTM A333/A333M, ASTM A334/A334M, ASME B36.10M. Equivalent grades across ASTM, EN, DIN, JIS and GB/T standards are indicative; we check them against each tender.

Materials

  • Tube: A333 Gr 1; A333 Gr 3 (3.5Ni); A333 Gr 6; A334 Gr 1; A334 Gr 6

Testing and documents

  • Charpy V-notch impact test, tensile, flattening, hydro or NDT (E213/E309)
  • Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection can be arranged against your inspection and test plan

Where it is used

  • LNG, LPG and ethane lines; cold-service gas-plant piping

Sizes

44 sizes, each under its own Indus part number in the size table. The sizes follow the standard's own table.

Ordering

Quote the Indus part number from the size table, or send the standard and grade, the outside diameter and wall (BWG or millimetres, minimum or average wall), the length and the quantity. We quote with the mill certificates and the inspection you need.
